question: What is the width of the court for double matches in Lawn Tennis?
solution:
The correct answer is __**36 feet.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Standard tennis court dimensions are defined by the **International Tennis Federation (ITF).**
 
• For doubles matches, the full court width is utilized, extending to the outer doubles sidelines.
 
• This width measures **36 feet (10.97 meters).**
 
• Singles matches use a narrower section within the doubles court, marked by the inner singles sidelines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tennis** is a **racquet sport **that can be played by **two teams **of **two players **each, or it can be played individually against one opponent.
 
• A** hollow rubber ball **covered in felt is struck by each player using a tennis racket that is strung with **cord over or around a net **and into the court of their opponent. 
 
• **Major Walter Wingfield **of Her Majesty's Body Guard created the game, which he first played in **1874** under the name** "Spharistike."**
 
• **Denbighshire, England** hosted the first-ever game, and the first-ever public competition happened in **1875.**

**Basic Rules**

 
• **Scoring System**: The match consists of points, games, and sets. A player wins a point when the opponent fails to return the ball within the prescribed dimensions of the court. Games are won by the first player to win at least four points in total and at least two points more than the opponent. A set consists of a sequence of games, with players alternating serves. Matches are generally best of three or five sets.
 
• **Serving**: Matches start with a coin toss to decide which player will serve first. The server must hit the ball over the net to the diagonally opposite service box. If the serve fails, the server gets a second attempt. A serve that lands in but is not returned by the opponent scores a point.
 
• **Faults and Lets**: A serve that fails to land in the opponent's service box is called a fault. If this happens twice in a row, the opponent wins the point. A let is when the serve hits the net but still lands in the service box, or a serve is disrupted by an outside influence – the serve is retaken with no penalty.

**Equipment**:

 
• Racket: Frame with tightly pulled strings.
 
• Ball: Felt-covered rubber.
 
• Apparel: Sportswear and tennis shoes.

**Key Terminology:**

 
• **Ace:** Unreturned serve.
 
• **Break:** Winning a game when opponent serves.
 
• **Deuce:** Score of 40-40; requires two consecutive points to win from this position.
 
• **Love:** Zero score.
 
• **Advantage:** Point after deuce; winning next point wins the game, losing returns to deuce.
 
• **Rally:** Exchange of ball between players.
 
• **Volley:** Hitting the ball before it bounces.
 
• **Groundstroke: **Forehand or backhand shot after the ball bounces.

**Governing Bodies and Tournaments:**

 
• **Organizations:** International Tennis Federation (ITF), Women's Tennis Association (WTA), Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP).
 
• **Grand Slam Tournaments:** Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, US Open.
